newsitem.title: CHINA: Earthquake in northwest China kills nine.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake in northwest China kills nine.

text.p: An earthquake jolted northwestern China's Xinjiang region on Friday, killing at least nine people and injuring more than 40 in an area rocked by thousands of tremors this year, officials said.
The quake measuring 6.6 on the Richter scale struck Jiashi in the northwestern Xinjiang region at 1.34 p.m. (0534 GMT), a local broadcasting official said by telephone.
"This earthquake was very sudden," the official said. "We had no preparation."
An official of the Seismological Bureau in the nearby city of Kashgar said by telephone that the toll would rise as rescue teams searched for survivors in remote villages.
Units of the People's Liberation Army were helping rescue efforts in the region, populated mainly by cotton farmers and sheep herders of the Moslem Uighur minority.
A large number of buildings were destroyed, officials said. Detailed figures were unavailable.

"There have been so many earthquakes here recently that no one dares to go home and we are all living in tents. The casualties this time were because buildings collapsed on tents nearby, one hospital official said.
"The earth never seems to stop shaking," she added. "But today the earthquake felt even stronger than before."

More than 4,000 earthquakes and aftershocks have jolted the region since January and Xinhua news agency quoted seismological officials as saying more quakes of a magnitude above six on the Richter were forecast.
At least 23 people were injured and thousands of buildings destroyed last Sunday by two large earthquakes in Jiashi.
Officials said no one was killed then, mainly because most people had been living out of doors in tents since an earthquake measuring 6.4 rocked Jiashi in January, killing 50 people.
An earthquake measuring 6.9 killed 24 people and injured 40 in Jiashi on March 20, just days after a tremor of 6.0 magnitude killed two and injured three.
"The quakes hitting the area have shown no obvious signs of decline in terms of magnitude in the near future," said scientist Ding Jianhai, quoted by Xinhua.
Ding, head of the Department of Earthquake Prediction and Analysis, added that it was rare for so many strong quakes to hit in the same place at such short intervals.
Jiashi county lies at the meeting of the Pamir-Lake Baikal seismological belt and the seismological belt of the Himalayas, making it vulnerable to frequent tremors, Ding said.
Three quakes measuring more than six on the Richter scale jolted Jiashi in 1961 and after-shocks continued for 20 months, he said.
